method: tools/flipper_pull.py (storage list/storage read over the USB CLI)
note: Only the captures this repo did not already hold were copied. The rest of the device tree duplicates research/sources/corpus_automotive_subghz. Of the four frame-less multi-MB RAW recordings, three were triaged on the card and dropped because they carry no frame: two older ones (20260927, 20260930) were never pulled, and one (20261005) is kept as a false-positive corpus in the development tree only and is excluded from the published tree (marked shipped_in_public false). Their hashes and structure are recorded here; the bytes are not shipped.

files.name: RAW-20260926-211319.sub
files.structure: STRONG repeat (99 symbols); 126 bursts separated by ~20 ms gaps; one uniform 1570-1630 us tone burst

files.name: RAW-20260927-091503.sub
files.structure: NONE repeat; 4539 bursts; edge-width density (65/99/131 us) with no frame

files.name: RAW-20260930-111914.sub
files.structure: NONE repeat (12); 12321 bursts; same width density as 091503

files.name: RAW-20261005-100939.sub
files.structure: NONE repeat; 12534 bursts on a 33 us ladder (65/99/131/165 us = 2T/3T/4T/5T); longest repeated run 22 symbols in 2 of 12534 bursts; no frame. Kept as a false-positive corpus, where all 44 shipped decoders stay quiet on it; the 5.9 MB recording is held in the development tree only and not published

files.name: decoded_key_files/
files.structure: Flipper SubGhz Key Files with the protocol, bit count, key and TE in the header: Ford V0 x8, BinRAW x7, RAW x3, Princeton x3, Fiat V0 x2, and CAME / Dickert / KeeLoq / KIA-HYU V3 / Korea v1 / SMC5326 / Security+ 1.0 x1 each. Known-answer vectors for the decoders the card already carries; Dickert and SMC5326 have no card decoder.
